title: 2022年12月四级真题 第1套 阅读1
paperTitle: 2022年12月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
passage:
P1 To write his 2010 book, The 5-Factor World Diet, nutritionist Harley Pasternak traveled to the healthiest countries around the world to learn more about what made their meals extra nourishing.

P2 He noted that Japanese people ate a wonderful variety of seaweeds, and that Chinese people tried to include at least five different colors in every meal. Pasternak also came away with some valuable observations about how different the North American way of life was, compared with many other countries.

P3 For starters, Americans eat much bigger portions than people in other countries. "We don't prioritize eating seasonally or locally, and we also add lots of salt, sugar and thickening agents to our foods," explained Pasternak. Contrast that to the healthy Mediterranean, Nordic and Okinawan diets listed in Pasternak's book. They all seem to stick to the ethos(特质) of regional, seasonal produce.

P4 For example, a traditional Mediterranean diet includes fruits, vegetables, whole grains, nuts and olive oil as the main components of nutritional intake. Fish, chicken and red wine make moderate appearances, while red meat, salt and sugar are used much less often. The benefits of a traditional Mediterranean diet have been studied since the 1970s, and researchers have found that living that olive oil life can help people lose weight, lower their heart disease risk and reverse diabetes.

P5 Most other healthy eating cultures also make meals an event—say, multiple courses around the family table, or a glass or two of red wine at a long lunch—as opposed to hastily wolfing down handfuls of cereal above the kitchen sink and calling it dinner.

P6 Each of the healthy eating cultures has its own unique feature. But Pasternak did take note of one unifying factor in all of the healthy societies he observed. "The only overlapping feature in most of these healthy countries is that they all walk way more than the average American," said Pasternak, "So really, regardless of what you're eating, if someone's walking four miles more than you each day, they're going to be a lot thinner and live a lot longer than you."

questions.q: What characterizes Japanese and Chinese foods?
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What characterizes Japanese and Chinese foods? 是 what 直接询问客观特征，没 有 infer/suggest/imply 之类的推断信号，要的就是原文写明的事实。

【拆句】题干 What characterizes Japanese and Chinese foods? 是标准的 what 主语疑问句： what 作主语，characterizes 作谓语，Japanese and Chinese foods 是宾语，结构平铺直 叙，无陷阱。 46. What characterizes Japanese and Chinese foods? A) Variety. B) Flavor. C) Color. D) Naturalness.

【定位】He noted that Japanese people ate a wonderful variety of seaweeds, and that Chinese people tried to include at least five different colors in every meal. 他注意到日本人吃种类繁多的海藻，中国人则努力让每餐都包含至少五种不同的颜色。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 a wonderful variety of seaweeds ↔Variety at least five different colors in every meal ↔Variety 预判核心是"多样性"，Variety 既能覆盖 variety of seaweeds，也能覆盖 five different colors，是把两条并列事实的最大公约数提炼出来的上位词，与预判一致。 B) 无中生有 定位句 He noted that Japanese people ate a wonderful variety of seaweeds, and that Chinese people tried to include at least five different colors in every meal. 通 篇讲海藻种类和颜色，没有任何 flavor/taste 的描述；选项 Flavor 在原文里没有对应。 C) 以偏概全 选项 Color 只对应 at least five different colors in every meal 这一半，根本不能解释 a wonderful variety of seaweeds——日本人吃海藻种类多与颜色无关；以局部冒充 整体。 D) 无中生有 Naturalness 意为"天然性、未加工"，原文定位句没有 natural/unprocessed/raw 之类 的词；海藻和颜色多样不等于"自然"。 美国人在饮食方式上的典型特点是什么? A) 他们强调营养。 B) 他们往往吃得相当多。 C) 他们优先考虑便利性。 D) 他们在意味道。

questions.q: What is typical of Americans in the way of eating?
options: They tend to eat quite a lot.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What is typical of Americans in the way of eating? 用 typical 直接问"典型"，要求 原文里被作者明确点出的美国人吃饭特征。

【拆句】题干主干是 what is typical of Americans，in the way of eating 是修饰 typical 的范围介 词短语；结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】For starters, Americans eat much bigger portions than people in other countries. 首先，美国人吃的分量比其他国家的人要大得多。 47. What is typical of Americans in the way of eating? A) They emphasize nutrition. B) They tend to eat quite a lot. C) They prioritize convenience. D) They care about flavors.

【选项】A) 与原文相反 原文 We don't prioritize eating seasonally or locally, and we also add lots of salt, sugar and thickening agents to our foods 说的是美国人"不"重视当季当地、还要加 大量盐糖增稠剂——明显是不健康、不重营养的做法，emphasize nutrition 与原文方 向相反。 B) ✓ 正确 eat much bigger portions ↔tend to eat quite a lot than people in other countries ↔tend to 预判核心是"美国人吃得多"，They tend to eat quite a lot. 把定位句的数量比较结论直 接保留下来，没做引申，与预判完全一致。 C) 无中生有 原文讲的是分量大、不重视当季当地、爱加盐糖——没出现 convenience/quick/fast/easy 等"便利"语义的词；选项 prioritize convenience 在原 文中无依据。 D) 无中生有 原文谈份量、当季当地、盐糖增稠剂，未涉及 flavor/taste；care about flavors 在原文 中没有对应表述。 地中海、北欧和冲绳饮食的特征是什么? A) 水果和蔬菜。 B) 橄榄油和红酒。 C) 时令本地农产品。 D) 未加工的食材。

questions.q: What features are in Mediterranean, Nordic and Okinawan diets?
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What features are in Mediterranean, Nordic and Okinawan diets? 直接询问几种 饮食"具备什么特征"，答案应是原文明写的共同特征。

【拆句】题干 What features are in Mediterranean, Nordic and Okinawan diets?：what features 作主语、are 系动词、in Mediterranean, Nordic and Okinawan diets 是表语介 词短语，把范围限定在这三种饮食里；结构清晰，无陷阱。

【定位】Contrast that to the healthy Mediterranean, Nordic and Okinawan diets listed in Pasternak's book. They all seem to stick to the ethos(特质) of regional, seasonal produce. 把这一点（指美国人的饮食习惯）与 Pasternak 书中列出的健康的地中海、北欧和冲绳饮食 对比一下。它们似乎都坚守着"当地、当季食材"这一特质。 48. What features are in Mediterranean, Nordic and Okinawan diets? A) Fruits and vegetables. B) Olive oil and red wine. C) Seasonal local produce. D) Unprocessed ingredients.

【选项】A) 以偏概全 fruits, vegetables 出现在 P4 段对地中海饮食的展开里；但题目问的是三种饮食的共有 特征，Fruits and vegetables 只是地中海饮食的成分，不能说北欧和冲绳饮食也以这两 样为主——选项错把局部例证当全局共性。 B) 以偏概全 olive oil 与 red wine 同样出现在 P4 段对地中海饮食的描写里，是地中海饮食的特色， 但不是北欧和冲绳饮食的特征；选项把地中海饮食的标志当成三地共同点。 C) ✓ 正确 regional, seasonal produce ↔Seasonal local produce 预判核心"当地、当季、食材"三层在 Seasonal local produce 中一一对应，无遗漏；这 是细节题正确项最干净的样子——预判几个要素，选项几乎逐词对接。 D) 无中生有 原文中谈到三地饮食的共同点只有 regional, seasonal produce（当地当季食材），并 未出现 unprocessed/raw/whole 之类强调"未加工"的语义；Unprocessed ingredients 是凭健康饮食的常识印象生造的特征。 大多数健康饮食文化中的人们有什么共同点? A) 他们让全家人在餐桌旁用餐。 B) 他们定时定点地进餐。 C) 他们早餐食用大量谷物。 D) 他们非常重视用餐。

questions.q: What do people in most healthy eating cultures have in common?
options: They get the whole family to eat at a table.
They eat their meals regularly and punctually.
They consume plenty of cereal for breakfast.
They attach great importance to their meals.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What do people in most healthy eating cultures have in common? 直问"共同之 处"，不含推断信号词，只要找原文的归纳句即可。

【拆句】题干 What do people in most healthy eating cultures have in common?：what 作 have 的宾语前置，主语是 people in most healthy eating cultures；have…in common 是固定搭配"有共同点"，结构无陷阱。

【定位】Most other healthy eating cultures also make meals an event—say, multiple courses around the family table, or a glass or two of red wine at a long lunch—as opposed to hastily wolfing down handfuls of cereal above the kitchen sink and calling it dinner. 大多数其他健康饮食文化都把吃饭当作一件"大事"——例如全家围桌吃几道菜，或者午餐时 悠悠喝上一两杯红酒——而不是匆匆抓把麦片站在水槽边解决一顿。 49. What do people in most healthy eating cultures have in common? A) They get the whole family to eat at a table. B) They eat their meals regularly and punctually. C) They consume plenty of cereal for breakfast. D) They attach great importance to their meals.

【选项】A) 以偏概全 get the whole family to eat at a table 只对应 multiple courses around the family table 这一个例子，没覆盖另一例 a glass or two of red wine at a long lunch，更没覆 盖"重视用餐"这个主旨；以一个例子冒充整段共性。 B) 无中生有 原文 P5 只说 long lunch（漫长的午餐），完全没有 regularly/punctually/on time 这类"规律/守时"的语义；选项 eat their meals regularly and punctually 在原文里无 对应。 C) 与原文相反 原文中 handfuls of cereal above the kitchen sink 是用来作"反例"的——讽刺美国人 草率吃法的——而选项 consume plenty of cereal for breakfast 反而把这条反例当成 健康文化的优点，方向南辕北辙。 D) ✓ 正确 make meals an event ↔attach great importance to their meals 预判核心"重视用餐"与 attach great importance to their meals 字字对应；同时这 一表达覆盖了原文后面三个例证（围桌、几道菜、长午餐），是所有例证背后的统一 主旨。 与普通美国人相比,健康社会中的人们___________。 A) 每天至少步行4英里 B) 步行明显更多 C) 更注重体型 D) 食用多得多的有机食品

questions.q: Compared with the average American, people in healthy societies ___________.
options: walk at least 4 miles a day
pay more attention to body shape
consume a lot more organic food
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 Compared with the average American, people in healthy societies ___________. 是补全句、内容来自原文的事实性对比陈述，不要求做推断，按细节题走。

【拆句】题干 Compared with the average American, people in healthy societies ___________. 是不完整陈述句：Compared with the average American 是过去分词短语作状语，逻 辑主语是后面的 people in healthy societies；选项是句子谓语的延续，需保证主谓搭配 自然。

【定位】The only overlapping feature in most of these healthy countries is that they all walk way more than the average American. 这些健康国家唯一的共同特征是：他们走路都远远多于普通美国人。 50. Compared with the average American, people in healthy societies ___________. A) walk at least 4 miles a day B) do considerably more walking C) pay more attention to body shape D) consume a lot more organic food

【选项】A) 偷换概念 原文 if someone's walking four miles more than you each day 中的 four miles 是 Pasternak 的进一步举例性数字，且是"多走 4 英里"（每天比对方多 4 英里），不是"至 少走 4 英里"；选项 walk at least 4 miles a day 把"多走的差值"偷换成"日行的总数"， 并加了原文没有的 at least。 B) ✓ 正确 walk way more than the average American ↔do considerably more walking 预判核心"走路远多于美国人"被 do considerably more walking 完整保留——比较级 more、程度副词 considerably（= 原文 way）、活动 walking，三层信息一一对应。 C) 偷换概念 原文 they're going to be a lot thinner 是"会瘦很多"——这是走路多带来的结果，不 是健康社会的人"在意身材"这一主观倾向；选项 pay more attention to body shape 是把客观结果错读成主观态度。 D) 无中生有 整篇文章谈份量、海藻、五色、当地当季食材、用餐重视度、走路——通篇没出现 organic（有机的）这个词；选项 consume a lot more organic food 在原文中完全无 对应。
